title: Temporal banding: modular focus controls for time-series annotations and concise SR summaries
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Problem: Our time-series charts have grown feature-rich (annotations, mini-legend, hover probes, streaming updates) and we are seeing a pattern of accessibility regressions and longer main-thread work in high-density dashboards. Users in low-power devices and screen-reader users report noisy, verbose ARIA output and janky interactions when many series and annotations are present.

Goal: Introduce a composable 'temporal banding' interaction layer that: 1) scopes keyboard and focus interactions into modular bands (overview, detail, annotations), 2) surfaces concise, single-line screen-reader summaries for collapsed bands, 3) defers heavy rendering (aggregation/resampling) to off-main workers and canvas fallback paths, and 4) provides token-driven theming so teams can opt-in to condensed vs expanded modes.

Scope: Design system-level component work and concrete changes to chart primitives (legend, tooltip, annotation rails, keyboard nav) including:
- Band definitions and voice-friendly labels
- Primary keyboard flows (Tab, ArrowLeft/Right to move time probe; Shift to jump bands)
- SR summaries for collapsed bands (1-2 sentences max) and ARIA-live polite updates for focused probes
- Visual affordances for condensed mode (reduced axis ticks, compact legend rows) controlled by design tokens
- Perf switching strategy: low-fidelity placeholders + progressive hydration + GPU fallback for long-series rendering

Proposed solution:
1) Interaction model: Implement 3 logical bands per chart instance: OVERVIEW, DETAIL, and ANNOTATIONS. Each band gets a simple roving tabindex container. Focus movement between bands uses Alt/Option+ArrowUp/Down (documented) and an explicit chevron affordance in the corner.
2) Screen reader behavior: When a band is collapsed, expose data-summary token that produces a single-line announcement (e.g., "Overview: 3 series, last point 1.2k, trend up"). When user focuses a probe, ARIA-live region emits a concise delta ("+14% since last probe"). Full verbose Narration mode is opt-in via token.
3) Performance model: Introduce progressive sampling pipeline: a) light-weight decimation on main thread for immediate paint, b) async resample on worker and swap in when ready, c) if WebGL available use GPU composite path, else canvas fallback. Expose a design token chart.rendering.mode with values [auto, cpu-first, gpu-first, low-fidelity]. Default auto uses heuristics (device memory, series length, battery).
4) Theming/tokens: Add tokens: chart.band.padding, chart.band.summary-font-size, chart.mode.compact-toggle, chart.legend.row-gap-compact, chart.a11y.announce-mode. Update token docs and usage examples.

Acceptance criteria:
- Keyboard navigation: full roving-tab behavior across bands documented and validated in DFARS-like keyboard-only tests
- SR summaries: collapsed band summary limited to 140 characters and passes quick NVDA/VoiceOver checks
- Perf: 90th percentile main-thread frame time under 50ms for a dashboard with 10 series of 20k points when chart.rendering.mode=auto on modern laptop; 95th percentile under 120ms on mid-tier laptop with low-fidelity mode
- Tokens live in design system token set and are plumbed to chart primitives in storybook examples

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- How opinionated should default summaries be vs allowing product teams to supply their own domain-specific text? Proposal: provide smart-default generator and explicit slots for a custom summary string.
- Runtime complexity: adding banding and async pipelines increases code complexity. We propose a feature flag gated rollout with telemetry to measure adoption and regressions.
- Mobile semantics: band-based focus patterns are less applicable to mobile touch flows; we need an alternate gesture set (two-finger swipe) and smaller summaries.

Telemetry & observability: instrument events: chart.band.focused, chart.probe.deltaAnnounced, chart.render.modeSwapped, chart.token.modeChanged. Add histograms for framesMainThreadMs and renderSwapLatency.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Provide a minimal API in the chart primitive: setBands(bands: string[]), bandSummary(bandKey, string | generator), renderingMode(token string)
- Worker resampling should accept sample-target (e.g., 1000 points) and return change sets rather than whole buffers to minimize message size
- Use requestIdleCallback fallback for low-power devices where available

Design deliverables:
- High-fidelity component states: expanded, collapsed, focused-probe, error/empty states
- Storybook stories demonstrating tokens: default, compact, high-contrast, and narration-mode
- Accessibility checklist and test plan

Risks:
- Users with custom chart implementations may expect different ARIA phrasing. Provide migration guide.
- Potential minor regressions for older assistive tech; will test across NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack.

Next steps:
1) Prototype SR summary generator and test with 6 screen-reader users (UX research) - owner: Jonah
2) Implement token set and Storybook examples - owner: Design System team
3) Partner with ENG to create worker resampling POC - dependency: ENG-9034
